requirements.requirement: inventory-api deployed as a managed systemd service on node1 and serving traffic
requirements.summary: systemd unit created with Restart=always, enabled and started; service reported active with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 on the running PID; curl to /healthz and /inventory returned correct JSON immediately after deployment.

requirements.requirement: Kernel OOM killer targets the memory-hog process rather than inventory-api when the system is driven out of memory
requirements.summary: Swap was disabled and an unprotected (oom_score_adj=0) memory-hog scope was launched, forcing a genuine kernel OOM event. dmesg directly shows 'Out of memory: Killed process 1773 (python3) ... oom_score_adj:0' and systemctl status confirms memhog.scope failed with Result: oom-kill, while inventory-api's PID (oom_score_adj=-1000) was left running.

requirements.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving throughout and after the OOM event
requirements.summary: The same inventory-api PID (1670) persisted across the OOM kill with a monotonically increasing uptime/request counter, and curl to /healthz and /inventory succeeded both immediately after the hog was killed and after swap/memory were restored, directly demonstrating the healthy-before/disruption/recovered transition.

requirements.requirement: The induced memory-pressure disruption (swapoff, memory hog) is reversed after the test
requirements.summary: swap was restored via swapon /dev/vda3 to the original 2GiB/0B-used state, and memhog.scope/script/temp files were removed and reset-failed, leaving no residual failed units or artifacts.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart boot identity/healthy state, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, recovered service/data state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (2db46909-...) and healthy inventory-api/swap state were captured; systemctl reboot was acknowledged; polling showed a timeout then recovered connectivity; post-restart boot_id (c1881a58-...) differs from pre-restart, matching the fixed after-executor snapshot; inventory-api auto-started (new PID, OOMScoreAdjust preserved) and both endpoints/swap returned to healthy state.

overall_summary: The executor deployed inventory-api as a systemd service with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, then directly demonstrated the required OOM-protection behavior: a genuine kernel OOM event (triggered via swapoff + an unprotected memory-hog scope) killed the memory hog (confirmed via dmesg and systemctl status) while inventory-api kept the same PID, an increasing request counter, and continued serving correct responses throughout and after the event. The disruption was fully reversed (swap restored, hog artifacts cleaned up), and the mandatory node-restart protocol was completed with a directly observed boot-identity change and full post-restart recovery of the service, its OOM protection setting, and swap state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. All state-changing commands are accounted for and tied to the task or its restoration, with one inconsequential failed command immediately corrected.
limitations: The interleaved output of cmd-84d44d7ae68648d0 (two /proc reads redirected with 2>/dev/null) required inference that the memhog PID had already been OOM-killed by the time the first cat ran, since only one process's oom_score_adj/oom_score pair appeared; this inference is well-supported by the immediately following dmesg/systemctl evidence but is not itself a first-hand read of the hog's live oom_score_adj value.

No steady-state throughput/latency measurement was taken during the OOM event beyond periodic curl checks and a request counter, so continuous availability during the brief disruption window is inferred from bracketing observations rather than continuous monitoring.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map to a clear purpose: service/unit creation for the task, swapoff/memhog launch as a bounded reversible mechanism to force a genuine OOM event, and swapon/rm/reset-failed to fully restore prior state. One state-changing attempt (cmd-68332f34ebbe4f4a, systemd-run with an invalid -p OOMScoreAdjust=1000 flag) failed with return_code 1 and created no unit or residue (0 loaded units confirmed immediately after), and was promptly corrected by the next command with the working invocation. The reboot for the mandatory restart protocol is an expected, task-independent mutation. Fixed after-executor snapshots show no failed services, healthy package state, and no unexplained residue beyond expected reboot-related artifacts (reboot.log, refreshed systemd-private dirs).
